section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section provides the header and date for the maamar for Shabbos Parshas Vayigash, 7 Teves 5725.
section.t: B"S.
Shabbos Parshas Vayigash,
7 Teves,

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the connection between the parshah and haftarah, noting that while the parshah emphasizes Yosef's superiority over Yehudah, the haftarah points to the future superiority of Dovid (Yehudah).
section.t: "And Yehudah approached him [Yosef]" etc.1,
And in the haftarah of Parshas Vayigash it is stated2,

"Take for yourself one stick and write upon it 'for Yehudah'... and take one stick and write upon it 'for Yosef'... and bring them close to one another for yourself into one stick, and they shall become one in your hand."
And seemingly, the connection of the haftarah to the parshah is that the content of both is the connection of Yehudah and Yosef.
But in detail,
In Yehudah's approach to Yosef
(in the parshah)
it is emphasized that Yosef was superior to Yehudah,
to the extent that Yosef was king over all his brothers,
including Yehudah,
And in the haftarah it is stated3,
"And My servant Dovid shall be king over them."
[And as explained in Torah Or4,
that Yosef is
[Yesod of]
Zeir Anpin and Yehudah is Malchus,
and therefore now Yosef is above Yehudah,
for in the order of the chain of descent,
Zeir Anpin is above Malchus
[and furthermore,
Zeir Anpin is the influencer to Malchus.
And this is "And Yehudah approached him and said, 'Bi Adoni,'"
for the explanation of "Bi Adoni" is that in Yehudah
(Bi)
the influence from Yosef the Righteous
(Adoni) will be drawn.
But in the future to come,
when the root of Malchus will be revealed,
which is above the root of Zeir Anpin,
therefore then "My servant Dovid shall be king over them."]
But from the fact that the verse "And My servant Dovid shall be king over them" is also in the haftarah of Parshas Vayigash,
it implies
that in "Vayigash eilav Yehudah" there is also the advantage of Yehudah over Yosef.
Except that what is emphasized in the revelation of "Vayigash eilav Yehudah" is the advantage of Yosef over Yehudah,
and in the haftarah, the advantage of Yehudah over Yosef.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that "Vayigash eilav Yehudah" represents the unification of the upper Daas and lower Daas, making them equal, as indicated by the gematria of the final letters.
section.t: And this can be connected with what is explained in the discourses of the Tzemach Tzedek5,
that the final letters of "Vayigash eilav"
"Yehudah"
are equal6,
for the matter of "Vayigash eilav Yehudah" is that Malchus
(Yehudah)
and Zeir Anpin
(Yosef)
are both equal.
And he explains,
that the matter of "equal" is like what is stated in Likkutei Torah7
in the explanation of the verse8,
"to do what is upright (hayashar) in the eyes of Hashem,"
that the matter of "yashar" (straight/upright) is the connection and unification of the upper Daas and the lower Daas,
the upper unification and the lower unification
(both of which are equal),
to become one in the other9.
For Yosef and Yehudah as they are in themselves,
they are
(like)
two opposites.
For in Yosef
(Zeir Anpin),
which is from above downward,
it is10
the upper Daas, where there is "yesh" (existence) above and "ayin" (nothingness) below,
and in Yehudah
(Malchus),
which is from below upward,
it is10
the lower Daas, where there is "yesh" below and "ayin" above,
and the matter of "Vayigash eilav Yehudah" is the connection of the upper Daas and the lower Daas.
[And this is what our sages said11
on the verse "Vayigash eilav Yehudah": "Vayigash" is nothing other than an expression of peace,
for the matter of peace is the connection of the upper Daas and the lower Daas12].
And like the statement13,
"And the children of Yehudah and the children of Yisrael shall gather together, and they shall appoint for themselves one head,"
for now14,
the service of the children of Yehudah is from below upward,
the lower Daas,
and the service of the children of Yisrael
[the ten tribes who belong to Yosef]
is from above downward,
the upper Daas,
and in the future to come they will be joined together,
to become one in the other.
